Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Fri Aug 28 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Dolly, located over the central tropical Atlantic.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

header WTNT34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT4.

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM AST Fri Aug 28 2026 
000
WTNT34 KNHC 280832
TCPAT4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Dolly Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
500 AM AST Fri Aug 28 2026
 
...DOLLY CONTINUES MOVING RAPIDLY WESTWARD...
...INTERESTS IN THE LEEWARD ISLANDS SHOULD MONITOR ITS PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM AST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.5N 44.8W
ABOUT 1145 MI...1840 KM E OF THE LEEWARD ISLANDS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 24 MPH...39 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1007 MB...29.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Leeward Islands should monitor the progress of
Dolly.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM AST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Dolly was 
located near latitude 14.5 North, longitude 44.8 West. Dolly is 
moving quickly toward the west near 24 mph (39 km/h) and this motion 
is expected to continue for the next couple of days. On the 
forecast track, this system, or its remnants, should be nearing the 
Leeward Islands this weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Little change in strength is likely during the next couple 
of days, and Dolly is forecast to degenerate into a tropical wave 
before it reaches the Leeward Islands.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
north of the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1007 mb (29.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Dolly can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4 and WMO header WTNT44 KNHC.
 
RAINFALL: Heavy rain from Dolly could affect the Leeward Islands
late Saturday into Sunday, with rainfall moving into the Virgin
Islands, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.  This heavy
rain may produce flash flooding within areas of higher terrain of
the Leeward Islands.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM AST Fri Aug 28 2026 
000
WTNT44 KNHC 280833
TCDAT4
 
Tropical Storm Dolly Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
500 AM AST Fri Aug 28 2026
 
There has been little change with Dolly overnight. The storm is 
producing a small area of deep convection near and to the northeast 
of the center, but dry air is entraining into the southern half of 
the circulation. The initial intensity is held at 35 kt, in 
agreement with last night's ASCAT data and the latest satellite 
estimates. Satellite images also suggest that the low-level 
circulation could be losing some definition.
 
The storm is moving rapidly westward at about 21 kt, and that motion
is expected to continue as it remains located to the south of a
strong subtropical ridge. The NHC track forecast lies on the
fast side of the guidance, as most of the models often have a
slow bias for weak systems in this region.
 
The combination of increasing southerly vertical wind shear, dry 
air, and Dolly's fast forward speed should limit any notable 
intensification. In fact, all of the reliable models show the storm 
gradually losing strength and degenerating into a trough of low 
pressure before it reaches the Lesser Antilles this weekend. 
Post-tropical positions are provided from 36-60 h given the risk of 
gusty winds and heavy rainfall, however, it seems unlikely that 
Dolly will have a closed circulation at those times.
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Heavy rains from Dolly or its remnants could affect the Leeward
Islands late Saturday into Sunday with possible impacts in the
Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday. This
heavy rain may produce flash flooding, especially in areas of
higher terrain of the Leeward Islands.
